title: Registan, Samarkand
summary: The Registan is the central public square of Samarkand in Uzbekistan, framed by monumental madrasas. The oldest, the Ulugh Beg Madrasa, was built in the early 15th century by Timur's grandson. UNESCO lists the Registan mosque and madrasas among the major monuments of the Samarkand property.

uncertainty.note: Start is the beginning of work on the Ulugh Beg Madrasa (1417-1420), the first of the madrasas on the square. The later madrasas were not dated on any opened page, so only the first is recorded.

as_recorded.value: Timurid period from the 14th to the 15th centuries

when.display: Ulugh Beg Madrasa built 1417–1420; ensemble still standing

importance.justification: Named by UNESCO among the major monuments of Samarkand, a World Heritage property.

sources.title: Samarkand - Crossroad of Cultures (World Heritage List no. 603)
sources.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

reviewer_note: Place pin only. No model: no sourced height for a madrasa was opened. Coordinates are from Wikidata (39.6547 N, 66.9756 E), because UNESCO's listed points for property 603 are not at the square. Only the Ulugh Beg date is confirmed; the Sher-Dor and Tilya-Kori dates are left out.
